ask: Build the machine-load brake as a standing part of claude-settings, on every device that installs it (Windows and Mac, no admin): at the moment a lane is about to start, the guard reads the machine's load once and sets how many lanes may run.
note: Building in the goal session (batch 4 of briefs/cleanup-goal-oct21.md, updated Oct 22 to match the rulings below). Your rulings, Oct 21: (1) every device that installs claude-settings, storage as well as CPU and memory; (2) accurate; (3) cheaper than the problem: no watcher, no timer, no per-tool-call reading, no log of its own. Ruling, Oct 22 (session question 1): busy keeps no lane count; it refuses a background spawn (an Agent or Task call that runs in the background, including one that omits the setting if background is the default) and any Workflow, and allows a foreground spawn, so lanes run one at a time. Full refuses every new lane. Ruling, Oct 22 (session question 2, your view: no fixed count): drop the claude process check (31 ran on Windows: 14 app helpers, 17 CLI); decide on memory and free disk as shares of the machine's capacity, CPU second. Design: inside guard.py on Agent, Task, Workflow and start_session calls only; ctypes system calls, no child process, no file. Memory (Windows GlobalMemoryStatusEx, Mac kern.memorystatus_level), disk (shutil.disk_usage), CPU (Mac os.getloadavg; Windows two GetSystemTimes reads 200 ms apart). Placeholder levels: busy at memory over 85%, disk free under 15%, or CPU over 85%; full at memory over 95% or disk free under 5%. The refusal names the reading and says to run the lane in the foreground. Any read error counts as normal. Tests: readings match the OS's own tool within a tolerance on Windows and Mac CI; zero child processes and under about 300 ms on the lane-start path; busy refuses a background Agent, an Agent that omits the setting, and a Workflow; busy allows a foreground Agent; normal allows all; red on main. Finding, Oct 22, unchecked: 17 CLI sessions ran at once on the Windows machine, likely some stale.
title: Machine-load brake: every session paces its lanes to the device's real load
why: Your idea, Oct 20, widened Oct 21: when the machine is loaded, sessions slow down; when it has room, more lanes can run. Incidents: the 15 spinning claude.exe workers of Oct 19, the q_max load report, and the Windows RAM climb to about 98% of Oct 21. Your caution, Oct 21: measuring and logging have cost more than the problem before.
